bullets.title: AVGO: Citi models $29.4B Q3 beat; Earnings debrief Sep 2; AI ASIC mix a margin headwind
bullets.body: Citi models AVGO F3Q26 revenue at $29.4B vs. consensus $29.241B and EPS $3.24 vs. consensus $3.22; AI ASIC mix rising from 38% to 44% of revenue drives ~80bps gross margin pressure. FY27 AI revenue guidance expected around $116B (below prior buy-side expectation of $130-150B). Options imply ±7.4% move vs. 8Q historical avg ±10.8%; crowding score 0.93 (most crowded). Citi hosting live video debrief Sep 2 post-earnings and management callback.

bullets.title: NVDA: Hedgeye's #1 long; Morgan Stanley flags $200B TPU risk; AI buildout stocks under pressure today
bullets.body: Hedgeye keeps NVDA as #1 long, citing 70% FY2028 growth guidance and proprietary data-center model that precisely predicted earnings; values at 11x CY28 EPS with 'depressed and cheap' levels. Morgan Stanley separately highlights Alphabet's $200B first-party TPU revenue opportunity as a potential competitive dynamic. NVDA -1.4% in semiconductor complex premarket on rising yields and oil-driven risk-off.

bullets.title: AVGO/NVDA: NVDA investing $3.5B in MediaTek via convertibles; Horizon Robotics targets NVDA minority share in NEV
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reports NVDA is investing $3.5B in MediaTek via convertibles with NVLink Fusion platform adoption. Separately, Horizon Robotics secured design wins from largest NEV OEM (mass production 4Q26) and management targets Horizon + OEM self-developed chips to hold supermajority of high-end autonomous-driving chip share by 2027, leaving NVDA with only a minority position.

bullets.title: DELL/HPE: DELL raises AI Server target to $70B+ FY27; Citi traders prefer HPE 60/40
bullets.body: DELL targets FY27 AI Server revenue of at least $70B (up from $60B prior), with an eventual path to $90B+. Citi's sales desk reports traders prefer HPE over DELL 60/40 due to HPE's networking strength vs. DELL's PC exposure drag. UBS hosting earnings recap calls for DELL (Sep 2) and HPE/NTAP (Sep 3) with analyst David Vogt.

bullets.title: CRWV/HUT/BTDR: Anthropic's $80B compute deals set $16M/MW/year pricing floor—60% above prior levels
bullets.body: Anthropic signed two 6-year compute deals totaling $80B (~$35B with Lambda at HUT's Texas Beacon Point site, ~$45B with Nscale in Virginia) at ~$16M/MW/year—60% above the historical $10M/MW/year average. Bitdeer (BTDR) corroborated this pricing with a 9MW Asian 5-year deal at the same rate. HUT +1.9% premarket on the Lambda deal; CRWV -3.3% in broader semi selloff despite being Mizuho's preferred data center play alongside WULF.

bullets.title: AMZN: Citi calls FTC suit a buyable dip; maintains $350 PT Buy
bullets.body: FTC and 22 states sued Amazon for allegedly raising advertiser prices without disclosure (estimated $20B+ overcharges via reserve-pricing since 2019). Citi views the weakness as a buying opportunity given AWS AI acceleration and retail tailwinds, reiterating Buy with $350 PT. Morgan Stanley notes AMZN trading at 20x 2026 EPS with the Internet sector rated Attractive.

bullets.title: META: Morgan Stanley keeps OW; $17B teen-engagement settlement seen as innovation catalyst
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley maintains META Overweight following the $17B social media addiction settlement. Teens are <1% of META revenue and Instagram teen usage (~1 hr/day) is less than YouTube's (73 min/day), so analyst argues settlement could unleash product innovation (MetaClaw, MetaAI upgrades, new subscriptions) and hurt YouTube/TikTok more. META also launched Muse Code tiered pricing ($5/$15/$50/month) out of beta.

bullets.title: MDB: Hedgeye initiates LONG with +30% upside on Atlas acceleration; FY27 consensus looks beatable
bullets.body: Hedgeye initiates MDB long, targeting 30% upside on FY28 EBITDA with no multiple expansion required. Atlas growing 37→45% platform attach in four quarters; $1M+ ARR customers up 26% to 402. Consensus models FY27 revenue at $2.96B (in-line with guide), implying ~16% 2H growth vs. ~25% in 1H—a setup Hedgeye views as too conservative. Morgan Stanley separately notes 2Q Atlas accelerating at +30% YoY with FY27 Atlas guidance of +26-27%.

bullets.title: ADBE: Citi raises PT to $301 from $228; achievable Q3 beat/raise setup
bullets.body: Citi raised ADBE price target to $301 from $228, citing an achievable Q3 beat/raise despite ongoing Creative Cloud pressure and a 26% 2H NNARR decline. The analyst views near-term setup as favorable heading into conference season.

bullets.title: TEAM: Citi raises PT to $225 from $170 on AI 'Winner' designation and incremental demand metrics
bullets.body: Citi raised Atlassian's price target to $225 from $170, citing better sentiment, AI winner status, and incremental demand/workflow expansion metrics. The note cautions that the broader software rebound (IGV +47% since April) is more positioning-driven than fundamental, and median software names still expected to decelerate.

bullets.title: SNOW/NOW/CRM: Citi vol desk bullish ahead of SNOW earnings; NOW and CRM grinding higher on software rotation
bullets.body: Citi expects SNOW to beat by 4%+ with a 2pt FY27 raise; options imply ±11% vs. 8Q avg ±17%; stock up 89% since May earnings. NOW up 60% from July lows with avg sell-side PT $143 (3.5% below current) yet 90% Buy ratings. CRM 25%+ one-day rally followed by continued grind higher; Citi views it as having retail love and catch-up potential into Dreamforce/Analyst Day.

bullets.title: HOOD: Morgan Stanley upgrades to Overweight; raises 2026-28 EPS 12-15%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley upgraded Robinhood to Overweight, raising 2026-28 EPS estimates 12-15% on prediction-market traction and platform assets up 32% YoY to $369B. Stock +1.6% in premarket.

bullets.title: DUOL: DA Davidson raises PT to $175; 3Q DAU tracking accelerating to 25.6-27.6% Y/Y
bullets.body: DA Davidson raised DUOL price target to $175 from $160, reiterated Buy, citing proprietary tracking of 450K+ user profiles showing 3Q DAU growth of 25.6-27.6% YoY—accelerating from 23.1% in 2Q. Final week of August showed 1.8% WoW DAU growth, strongest since early June; firm's model has historically underestimated reported results by 100-200bps.

bullets.title: AAPL: Hedgeye flips to Short with 23% downside; services price hikes add near-term drag
bullets.body: Hedgeye flipped AAPL from long to short, citing 23% downside and iPhone price hike risk of 10-23% from China sourcing. AAPL also raised Apple TV to $14.99/mo (from $12.99) and Apple One to $21.95/mo (from $19.95), with iPhone 18 expected to carry a $100-200 price increase. Stryker's FDA-authorized SportSuite Vision for Apple Vision Pro is a minor positive catalyst for surgical use cases.

bullets.title: TSLA: Hedgeye short on zero-day call leverage; Cybercab event Sep 3 creating rideshare overhang
bullets.body: Hedgeye characterizes TSLA as a short setup, citing gargantuan leverage in zero-day calls as a behavioral bubble signal. Separately, Citi notes rideshare weakness (UBER) tied to Waymo's Atlanta expansion and the upcoming TSLA Cybercab event Sep 3 (TSLA currently operating ~200 autonomous vehicles without safety drivers).

bullets.title: DLR/EQIX: Mizuho and Kleintech both bullish; NIMBY headwinds seen peaking into midterms before YE rip
bullets.body: Mizuho remains bullish on DLR and EQIX, arguing regulatory pushback on new data center supply makes existing assets more valuable as AI demand outpaces capacity. Klein's desk echoes this view—9 states have pending moratoriums and 20+ have restrictive legislation, but NIMBY negativity expected to peak in October ahead of November elections before fading into year-end as concessions are made.

bullets.title: LITE vs COHR: LITE outperforming by ~2000bps; TSEM and MTSI flagged as top SMID longs
bullets.body: Klein's desk notes LITE +10% vs. COHR +1% in 5 trading days following LITE's stronger beat/raise in mid-August earnings. TSEM flagged as best long-term fundamentals outside NVDA despite being down 23% on no news; bulls see $14-15 CY28 EPS at $205 price. MTSI delivered 50%+ annual EPS growth with $12+ CY28 EPS power, trading at 22x forward.

bullets.title: MRVL/INTC/CRWV: Semis broadly under pressure premarket; MRVL remains Hedgeye long on Google warrant thesis
bullets.body: MRVL -3.6%, INTC -3.1%, CRWV -3.3%, and IREN -3.5% in premarket as semis sell off on rising yields and oil. Hedgeye keeps MRVL as a long, noting it is the first semiconductor company to receive Google warrants, confirming the XPU-attach thesis. Citi notes MRVL hit its October earnings bogey but missed margins and hasn't recovered.

bullets.title: CIEN: Reports Sep 3; consensus $1.64B revenue, options imply ±11.8% move; stock +38% YTD
bullets.body: CIEN Q3 consensus revenue $1.64B vs. guidance $1.575B-$1.675B; EPS $1.73; gross margin 45%. Stock up 38.3% since June 3 vs. S&P +1.8%. Options imply ~11.8% post-earnings move; last 4 quarter moves: -14%, -13%, +9%, +23%.

bullets.title: SHOP: Down 1.9% in Canadian trading; Hedgeye top signal-strength long list
bullets.body: SHOP -1.9% in Canadian premarket trading amid broader risk-off. Separately, Hedgeye includes SHOP on its top signal-strength longs list alongside SNOW, NET, MSFT, NFLX, U, and ABNB, ranked by time held in the portfolio.
